blocks.x: What Cyber & Zero-Trust changes inside Energy & Utilities: the processes we target, the controls we inherit, the platforms underneath, and the measured delta at every gate.

In Energy & Utilities, cybersecurity & zero-trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, ai-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (soc 2, iso 27001, pci dss, dora) that regulated industries must evidence. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: zero-trust architecture & implementation, threat intelligence & managed soc, identity & access modernization — delivered on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: IT/OT convergence, remote access growth and legacy SCADA estates create attack paths with physical consequences; CIP/NIS2 duties expand faster than programs mature.
Renewable supply and flexible demand make legacy forecasting blind; imbalance costs and curtailment climb while forecasts run on yesterday's methods.
Turbines, transformers and pipelines hold decades of life left — and zero telemetry. Condition-based maintenance is impossible without sensing, and failures cost the most when they are unscheduled.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

7 services from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower make up the delivery pattern — Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation, Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC, Identity & Access Modernization, Cloud Security & Posture Management as the usual core — run through the Dataq Method with DORA / NIS2 obligations baked into the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Never trust, always verify: zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Detection that keeps pace: intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Identity as the perimeter: workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
IEC 62443 zones-and-conduits with monitoring and access control (flat OT networks eliminated with evidence)
Restoration-tested backups and manual-fallback procedures (cyber events rehearsed as outages)

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: DORA / NIS2 and Data-privacy regimes. Smart-meter and consumer-energy data duties. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Programs run on the fixed rhythm below, chosen so progress is legible from week one. The first quarter of the rhythm is verification: weeks 1–2 measure the current metric with your team and lock it by signature. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with your control owner receiving evidence weekly. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and the measured delta against the signed baseline. Gates are binding: miss one and the program stops or redirects with a documented decision.
